column1: # EVERY point across all four Phase 29 plans where a real key, a real account or
# a real published release was the ONLY missing input. Each is individually
# citable with its exact substitution point, so a reader knows precisely what
# changes on the day a real key exists.
# NONE of these is graded MET anywhere in this phase. Not one of them was
# simulated, stubbed, or worked around, and no gate in any of the four plans
# could be passed by supplying one.

F29-LIMIT-01::REAL-KEY::substitution=RELEASE_TRUST_ROOT_JSON in crates/wcore-cli/src/update_trust.rs ships an EMPTY keys array and ReleaseVerifier::bundled() refuses it. Replace it with the real FerroxLabs release trust root (PUBLIC halves only, role release_acceptance, valid_from at or before the first release it vouches for), as produced by `wayland-release trust-root-init`. Until then `self-update` installs NOTHING. This is open HIGH F29-03-01 and seam request SR-29-11.

F29-LIMIT-02::REAL-RELEASE::substitution=.github/workflows/release.yml must publish a `wayland-core-vX.Y.Z-release-manifest.json` asset built by `wayland-release manifest-build` and signed by `wayland-release manifest-sign`. Measured by 29-03: release v0.12.25 publishes 7 assets and none is a release manifest. Second half of open HIGH F29-03-01; seam request SR-29-9.

F29-LIMIT-03::REAL-KEY::substitution=INDEX_PUBKEY_HEX in crates/wcore-cli/src/plugin/index.rs is still the all-zeros placeholder (finding F-021). This is the RUNTIME install-time trust root for third-party plugins, owned by Phase 25, and it is why Success Criterion 3's plugin clause and Success Criterion 2's plugin/backend clause are not MET. Seam request SR-29-8.

F29-LIMIT-04::REAL-RELEASE::substitution=the ACCEPT path of `gh attestation verify` against the real Sigstore transparency log needs a real published release whose archive carries an attestation, plus a `gh` that can reach the log. Phase 29 proved only the fail-closed paths; the accept path has NEVER been observed by this phase. Directly bounds Success Criterion 1's provenance clause.

F29-LIMIT-05::REAL-RELEASE::substitution=an end-to-end INSTALL of a real signed artifact -- download, archive-digest binding, attestation verification, extraction and atomic swap -- needs a published release NEWER than the running binary AND carrying a manifest signed by a key in the bundled root. F29-LIMIT-01 and F29-LIMIT-02 must both be satisfied first. No synthetic substitute was accepted for this.

F29-LIMIT-06::REAL-KEY::substitution=the release-acceptance ROLE KEY is Sean's by design and this lane neither holds it nor requests it. Run A completed the four-state chain with a key generated at run time into a temp directory that died with the run. That proves the MECHANISM. It is not a release acceptance and must never be read as one.

F29-LIMIT-07::REAL-KEY::substitution=a CI-SIGNED evaluation receipt. Measured this lane: `wayland-receipt sign` REFUSES to mint a CI authority claim over the fixture receipt -- "fixture digest is a synthetic binary/scenario label, not fixture provenance" (run-a-phase28-seam.txt). That guard is correct and was not bypassed, so run A's certification binding names a LOCAL-authority receipt and says so in its receipt_signing_key_id field. A real binding needs a CI-signed receipt from a real evaluation run.

F29-LIMIT-08::REAL-RELEASE::substitution=Phase 28's certification receipts on real native hardware, plus requirement R28-A -- a packaged-artifact list binding each distributed ARCHIVE by name and digest. `identity.binary_sha256` is the EXTRACTED binary; Sigstore attests the ARCHIVE; nothing in the tree binds the two. Until R28-A lands, a release manifest cannot honestly claim the certified candidate is the artifact users download. Seam request SR-29-1.
